introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Food and Nutrition 2 (0540), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS.

You are reminded of the necessity of good English and orderly presentation of work. Tabulate wherever possible and use diagrams where appropriate.
incertitudes: Règle de choix : la page de garde imprime « ANSWER ANY FOUR QUESTIONS » (4 sur 6 questions imprimées), sans section et sans mention « only the first four will be marked ». `groupes` = ["PAPER 2"] et `regles_choix` = parmi 4 sur 6, identiques dans les 6 fichiers.

Sujet scanné de 3 pages (page de garde, questions 1 à 4, questions 5 et 6), lu en image ; aucun schéma ni figure imprimé, donc `figures` vide dans tous les fichiers. Filigranes (gcerevision.com, Kawlo) ignorés. L'en-tête imprimé « Food And Nutrition 2 » est recopié en « Food and Nutrition 2 » dans l'introduction.

Points : chaque question imprime « Total = (25 marks) » ; les points imprimés des sous-questions totalisent bien 25 pour chacune des 6 questions (aucun écart). Pour 2(a), 5(a) et 6(b), `points` de la sous-question est la somme des parties (i) et (ii) imprimées (2+5, 2+5, 3+5).

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées au nombre exact d'éléments demandés. D'autres réponses sont valables pour les questions de liste ; le barème d'un point par élément est une hypothèse (le sujet ne le détaille pas). Aucune teneur nutritive chiffrée n'est avancée, sauf l'énergie d'un gramme de lipide (environ 37 kJ, valeur du programme).

Question 1(e) « mechanical raising agents » : le programme n'en nomme usuellement que deux (l'air et la vapeur), le sujet en demande quatre. Le corrigé donne quatre procédés mécaniques distincts (air par tamisage, par crémage, par fouettage, et vapeur) ; d'autres manuels répondent autrement (battage, pliage, laminage). À relire par un enseignant de Food and Nutrition.

Faits de cours à relire par un enseignant : les objectifs alimentaires de 5(b) (le sujet n'en impose aucun), les causes de faible production de 5(c) et les points de 6(d) sont des listes de manuel ; plusieurs autres réponses seraient acceptées.

Fautes d'impression du sujet recopiées telles quelles : « five (5) importance » au singulier (1d, 2a ii, 2d, 4d), « (5marks) », « (8marks) », « Recall three (3) advantages », « Pick out three (3) advantages ... of microwave cooking » sans point final, « Outline three (3) advantages and two (2) disadvantages of boiling » sans point final, « Define invitation ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
Pick out three (3) advantages and three (3) disadvantages of microwave cooking

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Microwave cooking** is cooking food in an electric oven in which microwaves heat the water in the food.

| Advantages (3 marks) | Disadvantages (3 marks) |
|---|---|
| 1. It is **very fast**, so time and electricity are saved. | 1. It **does not brown or crisp** food, so some dishes (roasts, pastry, fried foods) look and taste less attractive. |
| 2. **Little water is used**, so more colour, flavour and vitamins are kept in the food. | 2. Cooking may be **uneven**, leaving cold spots in the food, which is a risk if the food is not fully cooked. |
| 3. It is **clean and easy to use**: food can be cooked and served in the same dish, which reduces washing-up, and it is useful for reheating and defrosting. | 3. The oven is **expensive to buy**, needs electricity, and **metal containers or foil cannot be used** in it. |

questions.enonce_markdown:
i. List three (3) advantages of time management in the kitchen.

(3 marks)

ii. Give five (5) functions of fats in the body.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**i. Three advantages of time management in the kitchen (1 mark each).**

1. **The meal is ready and served on time**, and all the dishes are ready together and served hot.
2. **Time, energy and fuel are saved**, and the cook is less tired and under less stress.
3. **There is less waste and fewer mistakes** (no burnt or overcooked food), and more time is left for other activities.

**ii. Five functions of fats in the body (1 mark each).**

1. **They supply a large amount of energy** (about 37 kJ in each gram, more than twice as much as carbohydrate or protein).
2. **They insulate the body**: a layer of fat under the skin keeps the body warm.
3. **They protect and support delicate organs** such as the kidneys and the heart.
4. **They carry the fat-soluble vitamins** (A, D, E and K) and supply essential fatty acids.
5. **They are stored as an energy reserve** in the body, and they make a meal satisfying so that hunger is delayed.
themes: fats and oils in the diet

questions.enonce_markdown:
Mention five (5) rules to observe when entertaining a guest.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five rules to observe when entertaining a guest (1 mark each):

1. **Welcome the guest warmly** at the door, and make him or her comfortable by offering a seat and a drink.
2. **Find out about the guest's likes, dislikes and dietary needs** (allergies, religion, illness) before choosing the menu.
3. **Prepare the meal in time and serve it well**: the room and the table should be clean and neatly laid, and the guest is served first.
4. **Be attentive and polite**: talk to the guest, do not leave him or her alone, and offer more food without forcing.
5. **Be clean and tidy yourself, and thank the guest for coming**, seeing him or her off politely at the end of the visit.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Choose six (6) points to consider when preparing food for convalescence.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **convalescent** is a person who is recovering from an illness or an operation. Six points to consider when preparing food for him or her (1 mark each):

1. **The food must be easy to digest** - light, soft and not fatty, fried or highly spiced.
2. **It must be nutritious**, rich in protein, vitamins and mineral salts to repair the body tissues and to restore strength.
3. **Small meals at regular, frequent intervals** are given, because the appetite is poor and a large plate may put the person off.
4. **The food must look attractive and appetising**, with a variety of colour and flavour, and be served neatly on a clean tray at the right temperature.
5. **The advice of the doctor or dietitian must be followed**, including any food that the person must avoid.
6. **Hygiene must be strict** in preparing, cooking and serving, and the person's likes and dislikes should be respected; plenty of fluids are offered.
